alignments.note: The first colon is a verbless clause whose predicate is the fronted prepositional phrase `בְּאוֹר־פְּנֵי־מֶלֶךְ`, with `חַיִּים` as its postposed subject, so the construction-supplied copula joins the preposition heading that predicate under rule 49 and the unit heads on *In*. Rule 49 and rule 20 both direct that the Hebrew clause, not the English word order, decides which side is the predicate: the ASV writes *is* beside *life* by English locative inversion, and a copula standing beside the subject is not thereby the subject's. The unit is discontinuous under rule 25. This restores the treatment the same chapter gives every other fronted prepositional predicate — `וּמֵיְהוָה מַעֲנֵה לָשׁוֹן` → *is from Jehovah* at PRO.16.1 and `וּמֵיְהוָה כָּל־מִשְׁפָּטוֹ` → *is of Jehovah* at PRO.16.33. The competing reading makes `חַיִּים` a nominal predicate with the prepositional phrase as an adjunct and keeps the copula on the noun, but that leaves the clause with no subject at all, which rule 49's closing paragraph does not contemplate.
Construct noun with a supplied *the* under rule 29, no article morpheme being present.
Construct noun taking the chain's *of* under rule 19, discontinuous around the English possessive under rule 25.
Rectum rendered as an English possessive; the determiner of a possessive expression stands before the possessor's word and joins it under rule 29.
The clause's subject noun takes only its own English, the copula having gone to the prepositional predicate under rules 20 and 49.
Suffix rendered by the possessive *his* under rule 18.
Prepositional predicate of the second colon's verbless clause takes the construction-supplied copula under rule 49, headed on the preposition.
Construct noun with its indefinite article under rule 15.

Rectum takes *of* under rule 19 with a supplied *the* under rule 15; *the latter rain* is one substantive's rendering, headed on the class noun *rain* under rule 31's tie-break, since the ASV writes *rain* alone for other words of that class and *latter* is its specifier. The competing reading heads on *latter*.

review_notes: Corrected: the copula of the first colon was moved from `חַיִּים` to the `בְּ` heading the fronted prepositional predicate. Rule 49's first sentence governs, and its closing paragraph excludes the nominal-predicate reading because no nominal predicate stands in the clause — `חַיִּים` is the postposed subject.

The chapter's other fronted prepositional predicates (PRO.16.1 and PRO.16.33) are already aligned this way, so the accepted reading here was the outlier and followed the ASV's English word order rather than the Hebrew clause.
